atoms.text: Supernovas are big explosions that happen when a star is dying. This means that a star begins to collapse. The collapse causes a lot of pressure to build up and eventually the star explodes outwards. These explosions are often so powerful and bright that they can be seen throughout the galaxy for days after the explosion. After the supernova, the core of the star is often left behind. This is called a nebula. Nebulae are made of gas and dust. The photo above shows part of the Eagle Nebula.

atoms.a: Which word in the text means to fall apart?

b: ++a big explosion that happens to a dying star

atoms.a: What is a nebula made up of?

instruction.text: Match the words to their meanings.

atoms.b: the core of a dead star made up of gas and dust
an explosion after a star dies
a large group of stars and space matter
